question: On the exact current real kappa corridor, does the declared kappa-dependent reference c_kappa have a uniform full-minus-half-line L2(a dQ) envelope for D=partial_kappa c_kappa, without differentiating the selected actual solution or the boundary functional? The pinned lambda slab is context only because c_kappa and D are lambda-independent.
primary_sources: NIST DLMF 10.25.1, modified Bessel equation; with nu=i*kappa and x=6*pi^2*exp(Q) it gives the inherited reference coefficient x^2-kappa^2: https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.25.E1

declared_conventions.base_rotating_state: y=(c_kappa,c_kappa,Q/kappa); the free part is skew and the perturbation norm is at most V/kappa
declared_conventions.variation_rotating_state: d=(D,D_Q/kappa); its forcing has rotating norm 2*abs(c_kappa)
declared_conventions.derivative_scope: two-sided partial_kappa in the corridor interior and the corresponding one-sided derivative at each kappa face; the fixed Q0 reference initial data are kappa-independent
declared_conventions.execution: exact SymPy identities plus python-flint Arb elementary balls at two precisions; no Bessel evaluation, ODE integration, quadrature, root solve, finite difference, sampling, panel or compact Taylor transfer

upstream_results.role: pins the exact current corridor and the declared c_kappa instantiation only; its actual-family Gamma_1 face signs are not reference-variation evidence
pins the selected fixed reference, Wronskian boundary convention and the base rotating-frame reference bound; its lambda derivative is not reused as kappa evidence

assumptions: The hash-pinned reference convention fixes c_kappa(Q0)=1 and c_kappa,Q(Q0)=0 independently of kappa, so its finite-IVP kappa derivative has zero Q0 data.
The exact corridor has kappa_left>0, allowing the rotating state scaled by 1/kappa and a uniform worst-case q_left.

Standard smooth parameter dependence for a regular finite linear IVP gives D=partial_kappa c_kappa on every finite interval; the reported full-half-line statement is then a weighted envelope derived from the displayed comparison.
The backward rotating-frame propagator is bounded by exp(integral V/kappa), while the D forcing has norm 2*abs(c_kappa).
Linear growth of the D comparison is square-integrable against a=6*pi^2*exp(3Q/2). The envelope is a magnitude bound, not an actual tail value or a sign.
